symptoms: Bright yellow patches alternating with green on young leaves
Severe yellowing and stunting of whole plant with reduced pod size
management: Spray Dimethoate 30% EC @ 1.7 ml/L to control whitefly vector
prevention: Seed treatment with Imidacloprid 70% WS @ 5 g/kg

symptoms: Sap sucking produces leaf chlorosis; vector of devastating yellow mosaic virus.
management: Spray Acetamiprid 20% SP @ 0.2g/L or Diafenthiuron 50% WP @ 1.25g/L; neem oil 10,000 ppm @ 2ml/L.

healthy_signs: Dark green trifoliate leaves with robust branching
Abundant pink active Rhizobium root nodules upon sectioning
Profuse flowering and well-set pods without necrosis or pod-borer entry holes
Erect stem with no vascular wilting
management: Remove and safely destroy severely infected plants to prevent field-wide spread
Spray neem oil (3000 ppm @ 3ml/L) or approved target-specific bio-pesticides
Ensure proper soil aeration through light intercultivation
prevention: Treat seeds with Rhizobium culture and Trichoderma viride prior to sowing
Avoid water stagnation through raised-bed planting or broad-bed furrow system
Practice 2-3 year crop rotation with cereals like sorghum or maize
Install yellow sticky traps and pheromone traps early in the season
